title: Budget Billing Rider — Availability by Customer Class and Rate Schedule
content:
# Budget Billing Rider — Availability

Budget Billing is offered at Lakeshore Power & Light Company through six plans, each attached to one Electric Service Agreement. Each plan is available only to the customer class and on the rate schedules listed for it below, within the demand, usage, service-length and past-due limits listed for it, and only on an agreement whose status is listed for it.

## Availability schedule — class, schedules and size limits

| Plan | Customer class | Rate schedules on which the plan may be held | Highest measured demand in the last 12 bills | Largest 12-month usage at enrollment | Months of service at the address before enrollment |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Residential Levelized Billing Plan | Residential | Schedules RS, RT and REV | 0 kW (no demand limit applies to residential plans) | 0 kWh (no cap) | 0 |
| Residential Budget Billing Plan | Residential | Schedules RS, RT and REV | 0 kW (no demand limit applies to residential plans) | 0 kWh (no cap) | 0 |
| Residential FlatBill Plan | Residential | Schedule RS | 0 kW (no demand limit applies to residential plans) | 36000 kWh | 12 |
| Commercial Levelized Billing Plan | Business | Schedules GS, GST and GD | 200 kW | 0 kWh (no cap) | 0 |
| Commercial Budget Billing Plan | Business | Schedules GS, GST and GD | 200 kW | 0 kWh (no cap) | 0 |
| Small Business FlatBill Plan | Business | Schedule GS | 25 kW | 120000 kWh | 12 |

A usage cap of 0 kWh means that the plan has no usage cap. A demand figure of 0 kW is the entry for residential plans, which carry no demand limit; for a business plan the figure is the highest demand measured on the agreement in its last 12 bills that the plan allows.

## Availability schedule — account standing and other holdings

| Plan | Agreement status in which enrollment is accepted | Largest past-due balance at enrollment | Past-due balance placed in an active payment arrangement disregarded at enrollment | May be held with a net metering agreement on the same agreement | May be held on a time-of-use schedule | May be held while a payment arrangement is active on the same agreement |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Residential Levelized Billing Plan | active | $0.00 | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Residential Budget Billing Plan | active | $0.00 | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Residential FlatBill Plan | active | $0.00 | No | No | No | Yes |
| Commercial Levelized Billing Plan | active | $0.00 | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Commercial Budget Billing Plan | active | $0.00 | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Small Business FlatBill Plan | active | $0.00 | No | No | No | Yes |

## Reading the schedule

- **Class.** The three Residential plans are available to residential customers only; the Commercial Levelized Billing Plan, the Commercial Budget Billing Plan and the Small Business FlatBill Plan are available to business customers only.
- **Past-due balance.** Every plan allows a past-due balance of $0.00 at enrollment. Where the "disregarded" column reads Yes, arrears that sit in an active payment arrangement are left out of that past-due balance; where it reads No, they are counted.
- **Arrangement holding versus arrangement arrears.** Both FlatBill plans may be held while a payment arrangement is active on the same agreement, yet arrears placed in that arrangement are not disregarded when a FlatBill is enrolled. The two columns answer different questions and each is read on its own.
- **Time-of-use.** Both FlatBill plans read No for time-of-use schedules; the other four plans may be held on Schedule RT, Schedule REV or Schedule GST where those schedules are listed for them.

## Illustrations on hypothetical agreements

- A business agreement on Schedule GD whose highest measured demand in its last 12 bills is 200 kW is within the Commercial Levelized Billing Plan and Commercial Budget Billing Plan limit; at 201 kW it is not. (Hypothetical demand figures.)
- A Schedule GS agreement whose highest measured demand in its last 12 bills is 25 kW is within the Small Business FlatBill Plan limit; at 26 kW it is not. (Hypothetical.)
- A residential Schedule RS agreement that used 36000 kWh over 12 months is within the Residential FlatBill Plan cap; one that used 36001 kWh is not. (Hypothetical usage.)
- A residential agreement with $140.00 of arrears, all placed in an active payment arrangement and nothing else past due, counts as $0.00 past due for the Residential Levelized Billing Plan and the Residential Budget Billing Plan, and as $140.00 past due for the Residential FlatBill Plan. (Hypothetical balance.)
